### Question [1]{.slide-num} of 4 {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

Which of the following equations correctly model the relationship between a circle’s Area $A$ and
Radius $r$ ?
<br>
(more than one correct choice)

<!--
  MULTIPLE-ANSWER QUESTION
  - Use type="checkbox" so more than one choice can be picked.
  - List every correct letter in data-answer, separated by commas.
-->
<form class="quiz-question" data-question="Question 1" data-answer="b,d">
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q1" value="a"> A. $A = (\pi r)^2$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q1" value="b"> B. $\frac{A}{r}=\pi r$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q1" value="c"> C. $A=\pi^2 r$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q1" value="d"> D. $A = \pi r^2$</label>
</form>

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
Demo of math diagrams

```{.tikz}

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1]
  \def\R{1.6}

  % ---------------- (1) Radius ----------------
  \begin{scope}[shift={(0,0)}]
    \draw[circ] (0,0) circle (\R);
    \draw[seg] (0,0) -- node[right] {$r$} (0,\R);
    \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
    \node at (0,-\R-0.55) {\small (a) Radius};
  \end{scope}

  % ---------------- (2) Area: the r^2 square ----------------
  \begin{scope}[shift={(4.6,0)}]
    \draw[circ] (0,0) circle (\R);
    % hatched r-by-r square in the upper-left quadrant
    \fill[pattern=north east lines] (-\R,0) rectangle (0,\R);
    \draw[seg] (-\R,0) rectangle (0,\R);
    \node[right] at (0,\R/2) {$r$};
    \node[below] at (-\R/2,0) {$r$};
    \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
    % r^2 call-out
    \node (lbl) at (-\R-0.6,\R+0.75) {$r^2$};
    \draw[callout] (lbl.south east) to[bend left=25] (-\R+0.35,\R-0.35);
  \end{scope}

  % ---------------- (3) Diameter ----------------
  \begin{scope}[shift={(9.4,0)}]
    \draw[circ] (0,0) circle (\R);
    \draw[seg] (0,-\R) -- (0,\R);
    \node[right] at (0,\R/2)  {$r$};
    \node[right] at (0,-\R/2) {$r$};
    \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
    \draw[dim brace] (\R+0.15,\R) -- node[right=11pt] {$2r$} (\R+0.15,-\R);
    \node at (0,-\R-0.55) {\small (c) Diameter $=2r$};
  \end{scope}
\end{tikzpicture}
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}
    % (left) one quarter of the circle: two radii and the chord between their ends
    \begin{scope}[shift={(0,0)}]
      \def\R{1.6}

      \colorlet{sqcol}{red!65!black}     % dark red: square sides
      \colorlet{circcol}{blue!65!black}  % dark blue: circle
      \draw[circ] (0,0) circle (\R);
      \draw[seg, dashed] (-\R,0) -- (0,0) -- node[below, font=\footnotesize]{$r$}(\R,0);
      \draw[seg, dashed] (0,-\R) -- (0,\R);
      \draw[seg]
        (\R,0)  -- node[below=0pt, font=\footnotesize] {$x$}
        (0,\R)  -- node[below=0pt, font=\footnotesize] {$x$}
        (-\R,0) -- node[above=0pt, font=\footnotesize] {$x$}
        (0,-\R) -- node[above=0pt, font=\footnotesize] {$x$}
        cycle;
      \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
      % C call-out pointing to the circle
      \node(Clbl) at (\R+0.8,\R+0.2) {$C$};
      \draw[callout] (Clbl) -- (45:\R+0.05);
      \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
      \node[align=left] at (0,-2.6)
      {$C > \:x+x+x+x$};
    \end{scope}
\end{tikzpicture}
```
:::

### Solution

**Answer: B & D.**
<br>
**B**: <br>
$$
\begin{aligned}
    \frac{A}{r}&=\pi r \\
    r*\frac{A}{r}&=\pi r * r \\
    A&=\pi r^2 \\
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
:::

::: {.carousel-item}
### Question [2]{.slide-num} of 4 {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

A circle has radius $r$ and diameter $d$. Which of the following equations correctly relate $r$ and $d$?
<br>
(more than one correct choice)

<form class="quiz-question" data-question="Question 2" data-answer="b,d">
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q2" value="a"> A. $d = \frac{r}{2}$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q2" value="b"> B. $r = \frac{d}{2}$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q2" value="c"> C. $r = 2d$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q2" value="d"> D. $d = 2r$</label>
</form>

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
The diameter goes all the way across the circle through the center, so it's made of two radii placed end to end.

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}
  \def\R{1.6}
  \draw[circ] (0,0) circle (\R);
  \draw[seg] (-\R,0) -- node[above] {$r$} (0,0) -- node[above] {$r$} (\R,0);
  \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
  \fill (-\R,0) circle (1.3pt);
  \fill (\R,0) circle (1.3pt);
  \draw[dim brace] (\R,0) -- node[below=11pt] {$d$} (-\R,0);
  \node at (0,-\R-0.55) {$d = r + r$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
Which is bigger, $d$ or $r$? An equation that makes the bigger one come out smaller is written backwards.
Test each choice with a real number, like $r = 3$ (so $d = 6$).
:::

### Solution

**Answer: B & D.**
<br>
Two radii make one diameter:
$$
\begin{aligned}
    d &= r + r = 2r \\
    \frac{d}{2} &= r
\end{aligned}
$$

**Why the others are wrong:** A and C put the 2 on the wrong side.
With $r = 3$: choice A gives $d = 1.5$ and choice C gives $r = 12$ when $d = 6$. In both cases the diameter comes out *shorter* than the radius, which can't happen.

:::
:::

::: {.carousel-item}
### Question [3]{.slide-num} of 4 {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

Which of the following equations correctly give the circumference $C$ of a circle with radius $r$ and diameter $d$?
<br>
(more than one correct choice)

<form class="quiz-question" data-question="Question 3" data-answer="a,c">
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q3" value="a"> A. $C = 2\pi r$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q3" value="b"> B. $C = \pi r^2$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q3" value="c"> C. $C = \pi d$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q3" value="d"> D. $C = 2\pi d$</label>
</form>

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
Circumference is a *length*: the distance around the circle. If you cut the circle and unroll it, its edge is a little more than 3 diameters long. That "little more than 3" is $\pi \approx 3.14$.

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}
  \def\R{0.8}
  \def\D{1.6}
  % the circle, sitting off to the left
  \draw[circ] (-1.6,\R) circle (\R);
  \draw[seg] (-1.6-\R,\R) -- node[above, font=\footnotesize] {$d$} (-1.6+\R,\R);
  \node[center dot] at (-1.6,\R) {};
  % the unrolled circumference
  \draw[red!65!black, line width=1.6pt] (0,0) -- ({pi*\D},0);
  \foreach \k in {0,1,2,3}
    \draw[seg] ({\k*\D},-0.12) -- ({\k*\D},0.12);
  \draw[seg] ({pi*\D},-0.12) -- ({pi*\D},0.12);
  \foreach \k in {1,2,3}
    \node[above, font=\footnotesize] at ({(\k-0.5)*\D},0.1) {$d$};
  \draw[dim brace] ({pi*\D},0) -- node[below=11pt] {$C = \pi d \approx 3.14\,d$} (0,0);
\end{tikzpicture}
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
Since $d = 2r$, try replacing $d$ with $2r$ in one choice and see whether it turns into another choice.
<br>
Also, a formula with $r^2$ gives *square* units (like ft²), which measures area, not length.
:::

### Solution

**Answer: A & C.**
<br>
**C** is the definition of $\pi$: the circumference is $\pi$ diameters long. Substituting $d = 2r$ gives **A**:
$$
\begin{aligned}
    C &= \pi d \\
      &= \pi (2r) \\
      &= 2\pi r
\end{aligned}
$$

**Why the others are wrong:**

- **B** ($\pi r^2$) is the *area* formula. It's the most common mix-up on the ACT.
- **D** ($2\pi d$) uses the "2" twice. Since $d$ already equals $2r$, $2\pi d = 4\pi r$, which is double the real circumference.

:::
:::

::: {.carousel-item}
### Question [4]{.slide-num} of 4 {.unlisted}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Question

Which of the following equations correctly give the area $A$ of a circle in terms of its **diameter** $d$?
<br>
(more than one correct choice)

<form class="quiz-question" data-question="Question 4" data-answer="b,d">
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q4" value="a"> A. $A = \pi d^2$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q4" value="b"> B. $A = \pi \left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q4" value="c"> C. $A = \frac{\pi d^2}{2}$</label><br>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="q4" value="d"> D. $A = \frac{\pi d^2}{4}$</label>
</form>

### Hint

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 1
The area formula you know uses the radius: $A = \pi r^2$. What do you replace $r$ with if you only know $d$?
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint 2
A $d \times d$ square around the circle splits into four $r \times r$ squares.

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}
  \def\R{1.6}
  \fill[pattern=north east lines] (-\R,0) rectangle (0,\R);
  \draw[seg] (-\R,-\R) rectangle (\R,\R);
  \draw[seg, dashed] (-\R,0) -- (\R,0);
  \draw[seg, dashed] (0,-\R) -- (0,\R);
  \draw[circ, blue!65!black] (0,0) circle (\R);
  \node[center dot] at (0,0) {};
  \node[fill=white, inner sep=1.5pt] at (-\R/2,\R/2) {$r^2$};
  \draw[dim brace] (-\R,\R) -- node[above=11pt] {$d$} (\R,\R);
  \draw[dim brace] (\R,\R) -- node[right=11pt] {$d$} (\R,-\R);
  \node at (0,-\R-0.75) {$d^2 = 4r^2 \;\Longrightarrow\; r^2 = \frac{d^2}{4}$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```
When you square a fraction, square the top **and** the bottom: $\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{d^2}{2^2}$.
:::

### Solution

**Answer: B & D.**
<br>
Replace $r$ with $\frac{d}{2}$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
    A &= \pi r^2 \\
      &= \pi \left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2 \\
      &= \pi \cdot \frac{d^2}{4} = \frac{\pi d^2}{4}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Why the others are wrong:**

- **A** uses the diameter as if it were the radius. That's 4 times too big.
- **C** squares the $d$ but forgets to square the 2. That's 2 times too big.

:::
:::

```{=html}
<button id="submit-quiz" class="btn btn-primary">Submit All</button>
<div id="quiz-results" style="margin-top: 1em;"></div>

<script>
  // Turn "b, d" into ["b", "d"] (lowercase, trimmed, sorted)
  function parseAnswers(str) {
    return (str || "")
      .split(",")
      .map(s => s.trim().toLowerCase())
      .filter(s => s.length > 0)
      .sort();
  }

  // Format ["b", "d"] as "B, D" for display
  function formatLetters(letters) {
    return letters.length ? letters.map(l => l.toUpperCase()).join(", ") : "no answer";
  }

  // Score the quiz on submit.
  // Works for both radio (single-answer) and checkbox (multiple-answer) questions:
  // a question is correct only if the student picked EXACTLY the set of correct
  // answers, with nothing missing and nothing extra.
  document.getElementById("submit-quiz").addEventListener("click", () => {
    const questions = document.querySelectorAll(".quiz-question");
    let score = 0;
    let details = "";

    questions.forEach(form => {
      const name = form.dataset.question;
      const answers = parseAnswers(form.dataset.answer);
      const picked = Array.from(form.querySelectorAll("input:checked"))
        .map(input => input.value.trim().toLowerCase())
        .sort();

      const correct =
        picked.length === answers.length &&
        picked.every((letter, i) => letter === answers[i]);

      if (correct) score++;

      details += `<li>${name}: ${formatLetters(picked)} ${correct ? "✅" : "❌"}` +
                 (correct ? "" : ` <em>(correct: ${formatLetters(answers)})</em>`) +
                 `</li>`;
    });

    document.getElementById("quiz-results").innerHTML =
      `<h3>Score: ${score} / ${questions.length}</h3><ul>${details}</ul>`;
  });
</script>
```
